title: 0 - Basic data versionning workflow with DVC
text:
Introduction
I wondered if there was some software that would allow to manage data files with the same ease (ease…) that Git provides for managing code files.
My quest quickly led me to find DVC, which stands for “Data Version Control”. The project website can be found at https://dvc.org/, and the GitHub repository is at https://github.com/iterative/dvc.
I gave it a go through a mini project, thus learning the basic workflow of DVC. In this post, I will try to explain what I actually did. I hope this can serve as a quick kickstart reference for anyone who wants to get learn DVC.


Goals of the mini-project
I am planning on reading and editing a few pdf books in the upcoming months. A natural idea to save my progress would be a versioning system, but since pdfs are binary files, I cannot use barebone Git for this, and this is where DVC makes its entrance.


Methodology
DVC is a command line tool just like git, and it is meant to be used alongside git according to a “workflow”. The workflow is as follows:

As usual, we first create our working directory, which I’ll call education, and we git initialize it:
mkdir ~/education
cd ~/education
git init .
Then, we initialize DVC in our wokring directory, which looks just like we do in git:
dvc init
Now, here is the idea behind managing data files with DVC:

say we have a data file ./book.pdf that we want to manage with DVC. Instead of adding ./book.pdf to git via our usual git add ./book.pdf command (like we would do with text files), we add it to DVC via a very look-alikey command: dvc add ./book.pdf.
This will create a new text file ./book.pdf.dvc (right next to where ./book.pdf is located) which will act as a “pointer” to the actual data file ./book.pdf.
I say “pointer” because the ./book.pdf.dvc file will contain a hash of the actual data file ./book.pdf, thus “linking” or “pointing” to the latter uniquely.
Then, since the ./book.pdf.dvc file is just a regular text file, we can add it to git via git add ./book.pdf.dvc, thus creating a commit that holds a light textual pointer that links to the heavy data file: ./book.pdf.dvc *> ./book.pdf.
At the same time, the moment we do dvc add ./book.pdf, in addition to creating the pointer file


The actual data file will be moved to a hidden directory .dvc/cache in the working directory, and the pointer file ./book.pdf.dvc will be added to git instead of the actual data file. bash     dvc add book.pdf

title: Knowledge base
text:
1.1 Research areas within scientific fields
Scientific fields (SFs) can be further divided into research areas (RAs). For example, the scientific field of Mathematics can be divided into the following research areas:

Mathematics > Pure Mathematics
Mathematics > Applied Mathematics
Mathematics > Computational Mathematics

title: Knowledge base
section: 1.2 The table of contents of the knowledge base
text:
1.2 The table of contents of the knowledge base
The table of contents of the knowledge base is automatically generated based on the structure of the knowledge base. It is organized by scientific field and research area.

1.2.1 A research area is loosely defined
It should be noted that a research area is loosely defined and can be further divided into sub-areas. For example, the research area of Mathematics > Pure Mathematics can be further divided into the following sub-areas:

Mathematics > Pure Mathematics > Algebra
Mathematics > Pure Mathematics > Analysis
Mathematics > Pure Mathematics > Geometry



1.2.2 The research areas can span theoretical and applied research
For example, the research area of Mathematics > Applied Mathematics can include both theoretical and applied aspects of mathematics.

title: Knowledge base
text:
2.1 Text and equations
Textual content and mathematical equations are certainly the most frequent type of content.

2.1.1 Textual content
For example, you can write a paragraph of text like this:
`` The riemann hypothesis was initially proposed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859. It is a conjecture about the distribution of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, which is a complex function that encodes information about the prime numbers. The hypothesis states that all non-trivial zeros of the zeta function have a real part equal to 1/2. This conjecture has profound implications for number theory and has been the subject of extensive research and study. ”


2.1.2 Equations
For example, you can find equations like this:
\[
\int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{x^{n-1}}{e^x - 1} dx = \Gamma(n) \zeta(n)
